rationale: The workflow runs a 4-Python-version matrix on Windows and reinstalls pip dependencies (pip upgrade, requirements.txt, plus capstone and keystone-engine wheels) in every job with no dependency cache. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) is supported by the literature pattern (reported VM-time reduction) and by a measured fork experiment that inserts actions/cache@v4 for pip between setup-python and pip install, saving about 9.2% elapsed time. Prerequisites are met: repeated dependency fetching across the matrix, no existing cache, and the cache can be keyed on requirements.txt plus matrix.python-version. The change only adds a cache restore/save step; all build/test steps, matrix, timeout, and triggers are unchanged, so coverage is preserved. No permissions are weakened and no privileged, publishing/deployment, or new network actions are added beyond the standard official actions/cache, consistent with the existing actions/checkout and actions/setup-python usage.
